title: Crash when calling get_argument_count() on a Callable after its target object is freed
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in: 
- 4.4 RC1 (on macOS and Linux, Standard build),
- 4.4 RC3 (on Linux, Standard build)

### System information

Godot v4.4.rc3 - Linux Mint 21.3 (Virginia) on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 (nvidia; 535.171.04) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-9600K CPU @ 3.70GHz (6 threads)

### Issue description

When calling `get_argument_count()` on a Callable after its target object has been freed, the engine crashes without any error message or warning. This happens silently, making it difficult to debug.
Other methods in the Callable handle freed objects more gracefully:

- `get_bound_arguments_count()` - returns 0, no crash
- `get_method()` - returns "test_method", no crash
- `get_object()` - returns <Object#null>, no crash
- `get_object_id()` - returns the ID, no crash
- `call()` - produces error: "Attempt to call function 'null::test_method (Callable)' on a null instance."

Only `get_argument_count()` causes a hard crash without warning.

### Steps to reproduce

- Create a new Godot project
- Add the following script to a Node2D:
```gdscript
extends Node2D

class TestObject extends Node2D:
	func test_method(arg1, arg2 = null, arg3 = null) -> void:
		print("test_method called")

func _ready() -> void:
	var test_object := TestObject.new()
	add_child(test_object)
	
	var test_callable := Callable(test_object.test_method)
	var arg_count = test_callable.get_argument_count()
	print("init_check: ", arg_count)
	
	print("is_valid before queue_free: ", is_instance_valid(test_object))
	test_object.queue_free()
	
	await get_tree().create_timer(0.1).timeout
	print("is_valid after queue_free: ", is_instance_valid(test_object))
	
	# The crash occurs when trying to get argument count from a callable with freed object
	print("Testing get_argument_count() - game crash")
	var freed_arg_count = test_callable.get_argument_count()
	print("This line won't be executed if get_argument_count() crashes")
```
